Subject: Renewal: EU data residency, APAC rollout & cross-region failover for upcoming term

Hi Lena —

Hope you had a good week. As we discussed on the call last week, the 12-month renewal for NordicHealth is coming up on March 24 and you mentioned plans to expand usage into the EU region formally and to evaluate an APAC rollout pilot later this year. I wanted to capture the renewal proposal and next steps so your procurement and engineering teams have everything in one place.

Key ask for this thread:
- Confirm EU data residency requirements (single-country vs. multi-country within EU).
- Confirm whether you want cross-region failover (EU primary with US failover, plus APAC read-only replication) or strict EU-only residency for all customer data.
- Confirm the capacity increase (we proposed +2 reserved GPUs for peak inference during remote monitoring workloads) and any term changes you want on caching/retention.

What we are proposing in the attached SOW:
- Renewal term: 12 months (Mar 24, 2026 — Mar 23, 2027) with an option to add a 6-month pilot in APAC.
- Capacity: 2x dedicated instances (p3-equivalent) for production + 1x staging pool.
- Data residency: EU primary tenant (Frankfurt region) with optional cross-region failover to US-east for operational continuity. If you require strict EU-only processing for regulated datasets we can enforce region affinity and remove cross-region failover for those data classes.
- SLA/credits: updated latency SLOs for the higher capacity tier and 99.9% availability for the Dedicated cluster.

Attachments: NordicHealth_Renewal_SOW_2026.pdf (summary + pricing).

Next steps I recommend:
1) Procurement confirms data residency policy (strict EU-only vs. EU primary + failover).
2) If EU-only, we will add contract language and technical controls to block cross-region egress for regulated datasets.
3) If EU primary with failover, we will schedule a short runbook review with Vivek for failover testing and a proposed latency test window.
4) Sign SOW via DocuSign (link below) and we’ll lock pricing and reserve the capacity.

Docs: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345/nh-2026-rnwl-47
DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/en/sign?envelopeId=ABC123XYZ

Happy to hop on a 30-min call with procurement + engineering next week — please suggest times that work for you.

Best,
Marissa

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the summary and the SOW. A couple of clarifications from our side:

1) Data residency: For our production PHI-adjacent workloads we need strict EU-only processing and storage — that means no automatic failover that could result in indexable model state leaving EU boundaries. For lower-risk analytics (anonymized usage telemetry) we are OK with cross-region replication for backup.

2) APAC rollout: We are actively pursuing a Japan pilot for Q3; timeline is approximate, but we will need a plan for read-only replication in APAC and an SSO integration with our IdP there. The pilot should not require a full Dedicated cluster in Tokyo but should be able to attach to a read-replica pool.

3) Capacity: The +2 instances look reasonable but can we see a cost delta if we keep caching enabled vs. disabled for the pilot? Procurement wants per-token cost numbers with caching on/off.

Procurement, can you confirm the internal approval timeline?

Thanks —
Lena Svensson
Head of Platform Engineering | NordicHealth AB

Hi Lena / Marissa —

Quick technical note on the proposed architecture and the cost delta with caching:

Architecture summary:
- EU primary: Frankfurt (eu-central-1) tenant with Dedicated GPU pool. KV cache and model state pinned to EU tenancy for PHI namespaces.
- Cross-region failover (optional): We use async replication of non-PHI artifacts to US-east for warm-standby. Failover is operator-driven (manual or automated based on a trigger set) and will require a brief period of degraded perf while KV caches warm up in the failover region.
- APAC pilot: Read-only replicate inference results to a Tokyo read-replica cluster; local read caching reduces 95th pct latency by ~30-40ms in our tests. No writeback for PHI datasets.

Cost delta (rough numbers for planning):
- Per-token baseline at current reserved capacity: $0.00065/token (gen-heavy, 2.5k tokens/session avg).
- With caching enabled (prefix & KV) for high reuse flows: effective per-token cost ~ $0.00042/token (roughly 35% savings for the same throughput).
- APAC pilot (read-replica + local cache): small fixed monthly (~$2,400) + per-token addl $0.00010 for cross-region replication bandwidth for non-PHI flows.

Testing and runbook:
- We recommend a 2-week failover test window in staging and a 1-day smoke failover test in production during a low-traffic window. We will provide the runbook and a post-test report.

I can join a technical call with your infra team — suggested slots next Tue/Wed morning CET.

Regards,
